claims.text: The third piece on Mondweep Chakravorty's SGit and Ruflo proof of concept is about a path, not a failure.
claims.quote: is about a path, not a failure

claims.text: The adapter compiles the four ABP rows into Ruflo rules when the server starts and checks each of its tools with a pinned copy of Ruflo's own policy evaluator in enforce mode.
claims.quote: compiles the four ABP rows into Ruflo rules when the server starts

value.unit: ABP rows compiled into Ruflo rules

claims.text: Steps 4, 5, 6, 8 and 11 pass through the gate, and every one of them did what the policy said.
claims.quote: every one of them did what the policy said

value.unit: steps guarded by the policy gate

claims.text: Ruflo's own command line writes the two facts straight into the SQLite memory file in step 3 and reads it in steps 9 and 10, and none of those calls passes the gate.
claims.quote: In step 3 it writes the two facts straight into the SQLite memory file.

claims.text: The author's README states the limit in his own words: only adapter tools pass through this gate, other shell and network tools are unaffected.
claims.quote: Only adapter tools pass through this gate. Other shell/network tools are unaffected.

claims.text: In step 3 the memory file is ordinary, unencrypted SQLite; the ABP adapter and the vault are not on this path.
claims.quote: At this point the memory file is ordinary, unencrypted SQLite.

claims.text: In step 9 Ruflo reads a plain copy that came out of the vault, and neither the vault nor the ABP is on this path.
claims.quote: Ruflo reads a plain copy that came out of the vault; neither the vault nor the ABP is on this path.

claims.text: What an agent with shell access would do with the same command line or any SQLite client was not tested; the code confirms the path exists and nobody tried to misuse it.
claims.quote: The code confirms the path exists; nobody tried to misuse it, and it was not the run's question.

claims.text: The gap is not a mistake in the test but a property of where this ABP is enforced, and the author documents it; using the command line is what makes step 9 convincing.
claims.quote: The gap is not a mistake in the test. It is a property of where this ABP is enforced, and the author documents it.

claims.text: A policy holds on the paths that pass through its enforcer, and nowhere else.
claims.quote: A policy holds on the paths that pass through its enforcer, and nowhere else.

claims.text: When this site's own agent was measured, ten of its eleven rules were kept by the agent choosing to follow them, and the one hard limit was a platform setting the policy did not list.
claims.quote: ten of its eleven rules were kept by the agent choosing to follow them

value.unit: rules kept by the agent's choice

claims.text: At The AI Conference speakers said policy must live outside the model; this run does that and fails closed, and the next lesson is that around every path to the data is the harder part.
claims.quote: Outside the model is necessary; around every path to the data is the harder part.

claims.text: The fix on the author's list of follow-ups is native plugin registration, so the same compiled rules run where Ruflo runs and the command line's memory calls are checked too.
claims.quote: What is missing is running them where Ruflo itself runs, so the command line's memory calls are checked too.

claims.text: Two other ideas, offered not as findings: keep the working memory file where only the adapter can reach it, or make the adapter the only thing that can decrypt memory at all.
claims.quote: Keep the working memory file somewhere only the adapter can reach, so the command line has to go through it.

claims.text: The README is candid that plaintext exists during staging and intentionally in restored workspaces, which is the trade that makes step 9 possible.
claims.quote: Plaintext exists during staging and intentionally in restored workspaces

claims.text: Every error reads the same on purpose: the server replaces the detail so as not to leak dependency errors containing private paths or credentials, while the gate's own message names the reason inside.
claims.quote: Do not leak dependency errors containing private paths or credentials.

claims.text: Decisions are not yet recorded: the evaluator returns a decision for every call and nothing writes it to a log.
claims.quote: The evaluator returns a decision for every call; nothing writes it to a log.

claims.text: An operator log naming the row that fired would turn each decision into evidence.
claims.quote: An operator log naming the row that fired would turn each decision into evidence.

claims.text: The vault goes nowhere yet: no remote push is performed, remote sync is a follow-up, and each checkpoint is its own SGit vault on the same machine.
claims.quote: Each checkpoint is its own SGit vault on the same machine.

claims.text: The file name changes because the adapter stages and restores every checkpoint as memory.sqlite, whatever the source file was called.
claims.quote: The adapter stages and restores every checkpoint as memory.sqlite, whatever the source file was called.

claims.text: Approval means stop because there is nothing yet to give approval with; the run proves the row blocks, and proving it releases with a named approver is the next test.
claims.quote: There is no human approval fulfilment mechanism yet.

claims.text: Between step 2 at run clock 00:11 and the first fact in step 3 at 00:39, 28 seconds of run pass in a few seconds of video, so one wait was trimmed.
claims.quote: 28 seconds of run pass in a few seconds of video

value.unit: seconds of run trimmed from the video

claims.text: Not a vulnerability report: no one tried to bypass the policy, and the author documents the path himself.
claims.quote: No one tried to bypass the policy; the author documents the path himself.

claims.text: Not that the run failed: every step the policy guarded behaved as written.
claims.quote: Every step the policy guarded behaved as written.

claims.text: The fixes are ideas: native plugin registration is the author's follow-up, and the other two are the site's, untested.
claims.quote: Native plugin registration is his follow-up; the other two are mine, untested.

claims.text: The code was read, not run, here; its tests and evidence are the author's.
claims.quote: Its tests and evidence are the author's.

claims.text: The video was published on YouTube on 17 October 2026, the code read at its commit of 16 October, and the analysis made by Claude from on-screen content and checked against the timeline and the code by the site's agent.
claims.quote: published on YouTube on 17 October 2026, made as a member of the

claims.text: Mondweep's page on ABP-governed SGit checkpoints was merged into Ruflo's main branch by rUv, the fifth piece in the series.
claims.quote: merged into Ruflo's main branch by rUv
